title: Instant Pot Chicken Pepper Rasam
equip: Instant Pot (pressure cook + sauté), small deep nonstick pan (tadka), mortar and pestle

items.n: tamarind, soaked in 250 ml hot water
salt (1 tsp), adjust at the end
garlic (6 cloves), skin on or off

steps.x: Rub the skinned thighs with 3 g salt and ½ tsp turmeric. Leave for 10 minutes while you do the next two steps.
Soak the tamarind in 250 ml hot water for 10 minutes. Squeeze it out with your fingers, strain, and discard the pulp. Quarter the tomatoes.
In the mortar, coarsely crush ½ tsp pepper, the cumin, the coriander seeds and the garlic. Coarse is right here, since you want texture and no paste.

Add to the Instant Pot: thighs, tomatoes, tamarind water, 750 ml water, 6 g salt, ½ tsp turmeric and the crushed base spices. Seal and cook on High pressure for 12 minutes. Natural release for 10 minutes, then quick release.

Lift the thighs out onto a plate. Mash the tomatoes against the side of the pot with the back of a ladle. Don't use the hand blender, as it will cloud the rasam. Pull the meat off the bones in bite-size chunks and discard the bones. Return about three-quarters of the meat to the pot.
Before any adult pepper goes in, ladle out about 250 ml of broth with the reserved chicken into a bowl.
Press Sauté. Add the 1 tsp freshly crushed pepper and the naatu sakkarai to the pot. Simmer gently for 5 minutes. Don't hard boil, or the pepper turns bitter. Taste and add salt if needed.

Heat the ghee in the small nonstick pan over medium heat. Add the mustard seeds and wait until they pop. Add the hing and curry leaves for 5 seconds. Pour half into the child's bowl. Add the dried chillies to the pan for 10 seconds, then pour into the pot.
Turn off the Sauté. Stir in the coriander. Rest the rasam for 5 minutes with the lid on before serving over hot rice.

notes: Consistency: this is meant to be thin. If it tastes too sharp, the tamarind is strong, so add 100 ml hot water and ½ tsp more sakkarai.
Storage: 4 days in the fridge, or 2 months frozen. Reheat gently and never boil hard.
Meal prep: portion the chicken and rasam together, and add the coriander after reheating.
Substitutions: tamarind paste, 2 tsp (10 g), replaces the soaked tamarind. Skinless thighs are leaner, so you can use 10 g oil for the tadka.
source: None. Adapted from the standard Tamil pepper rasam method.
